title: How the constitution has changed since 1997

titles.subject: Political Science
titles.leaf: How the constitution has changed since 1997

author: 665add3c97efa06f3bbae34f
chapter_outcomes: an overview of the development of the Constitution  through key historical documents:  o Magna Carta (1215); Bill of Rights (1689);   Act of Settlement (1701); Acts of Union (1707);  Parliament Acts (1911 and 1949)
the nature of the UK Constitution: unentrenched,  uncodified and unitary, and the ‘twin pillars’ of  parliamentary sovereignty and the rule of law
the five main sources of the UK Constitution: statute law;  common law; conventions; authoritative works, and  treaties.

The role and powers of devolved bodies in the UK, and the  impact of this devolution on the UK.  • Devolution in England.  • Scottish Parliament and Government.  • Welsh Assembly (Senedd) and Government.  • Northern Ireland Assembly and Executive.

How the constitution has changed since 1997.  • Under Labour 1997–2010: House of Lords reforms,  electoral reform; devolution; Human Rights Act 1998;  and the Supreme Court.  • Major reforms to the constitution since 2010, to include  the House of Lords, devolution, electoral reform and  human rights.

Debates on further reform.  • An overview of the extent to which the individual reforms  since 1997 listed in section 1.2 above have been  successful or should be taken further.  • The extent to which devolution should be extended in  England.  • Whether the UK constitution should be changed to be  entrenched and codified, including a bill of rights.
